I'm currently 5 episodes into Tokyo Magnitude 8.0. The premise of the show is that a magnitude 8.0 earthquake has hit in Tokyo, and it follows a brother and sister trying to find their way back to their home and find their parents, joined along by a woman heading in the same direction

Whilst most disaster-centered media involves following complete badass heroes going through massive set pieces doing nigh impossible stunts, Tokyo Magnitude feels more...human. It's not without its set pieces, sure, but it isn't about people outrunning a road collapasing between their feet. All of the main characters are very much vulnerable to everything going on, and it really captures the state of panic and shock caused by an earthquake fantastically. It doesn't feel like it is a show meant to be a popcorn-flick, it feels like a study on humans when everything goes to shit. You see people doing their best to look out for each other, whilst you also see characters doing their best to make sure they survive, not caring about anyone else. You see people putting on a brave face, who keep on going through the nightmare, whilst other people are crying from everything they know being ruined. The main characters actually do a good job being a sort-of smorgasbord of all of these emotions, whether being subdued or exaggerated, and they have been getting some pretty nice development so far. There's something which I find quite beautiful within the story that's being told. It's quite realistic, seeing all of the damage around the city feels so harrowing to watch, and the writing is quite impressive. I'm really liking Tokyo Magnitude 8.0 so far
